news.text: 11 October saw university law professor Anita Hill testify before the US Senate Judiciary Committee, providing sworn testimony accusing Supreme Court nominee **Clarence Thomas** of repeated sexual harassment. Televised gavel-to-gavel before an audience of millions, the contentious hearings ignited a national reckoning on gender relations and **workplace harassment**, though Thomas was narrowly confirmed by **52 votes to 48**.
news.youtube: Anita Hill Clarence Thomas Senate hearing October 1991 archival footage

news.text: 16 October saw 35-year-old George Hennard crash his pickup truck through the front window of **Luby's Cafeteria** in Killeen, Texas, before opening fire with semi-automatic pistols on lunchtime patrons. Murdering **23 innocent people** and wounding 27 others before taking his own life, the tragedy stood as the deadliest mass shooting in modern US history and spurred fierce debates over American **concealed-carry legislation**.
news.youtube: Lubys cafeteria shooting massacre Killeen Texas October 1991 news

news.text: 27 October saw WCW stage ***Halloween Havoc 1991*** at the UTC Arena in Chattanooga, Tennessee. While Lex Luger retained the WCW World Title against Ron Simmons in a two-out-of-three falls match, the event was immortalized by the surreal **Chamber of Horrors match**, featuring an enclosed steel cage with an electric chair, culminating in Abdullah the Butcher accidentally being **electrocuted by Cactus Jack**.
news.youtube: Chamber of Horrors match Halloween Havoc 1991 Abdullah electrocuted

news.text: 27 October saw the Minnesota Twins defeat the Atlanta Braves 1–0 in the tenth inning of Game 7 to win the **1991 World Series** at the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome. Often voted the greatest World Series ever played, 36-year-old pitching ace **Jack Morris** threw a legendary **10-inning complete-game shutout**, holding the Braves scoreless before Gene Larkin's walk-off single sealed victory.
news.youtube: Jack Morris Game 7 1991 World Series Minnesota Twins final out

news.text: 30 October saw the **Madrid Peace Conference** open in the Spanish capital, co-sponsored by US President George H.W. Bush and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev. Convening delegations from Israel, Syria, Lebanon, and a joint Jordanian-Palestinian group for direct talks for the first time in Middle Eastern history, the historic summit laid the groundwork for the **Oslo Peace Accords**.

gaming.title: Sid Meier's Civilization
gaming.reviewQuote: Just one more turn! Civilization is an addictive masterpiece of immense scope and brilliant design that will swallow entire weeks of your life.
gaming.headline: Chariots, Tech Trees, and 'Just One More Turn' Perfection
gaming.gameplay: Designed and programmed by **Sid Meier** and Bruce Shelley at MicroProse, *Civilization* launched for MS-DOS in October 1991. Tasking players with guiding a fledgling prehistoric tribe through 6,000 years of human history to conquer the globe or launch an interstellar colony ship to Alpha Centauri, the game pioneered the **4X genre** (eXplore, eXpand, eXploit, eXterminate). Players founded cities, researched branched technologies on the revolutionary **tech tree**, conducted diplomacy with historical leaders like Gandhi and Lincoln, and managed civic wonders of the world.
gaming.reception: Critical acclaim was ecstatic and universal upon release. Reviewers hailed its flawless pacing, accessible interface, and terrifying psychological addiction that coined the famous industry phrase **'just one more turn syndrome'**. Publications routinely awarded it 95% to 98%, placing it at the summit of strategy gaming.
gaming.impact: Selling millions of units and launching an ongoing multi-decade flagship franchise, *Civilization* remains widely cited by historians and critics as one of the greatest video games ever conceived.
